q.t: Which of these statements is correct?
q.e: Jane Austen's books include Pride and Prejudice and Sense and Sensibility. Her novels are concerned with marriage and family relationships. Charles Dickens wrote Oliver Twist and Great Expectations.
o: Jane Austen wrote Sense and Sensibility
Charles Dickens wrote Sense and Sensibility

q.t: Which TWO characters from the books of Charles Dickens are referred to in everyday talk?
q.e: Charles Dickens wrote a number of very famous novels, including Oliver Twist and Great Expectations. You will hear references in everyday talk to some of the characters in his books, such as Scrooge, a mean person, or Mr Micawber, always hopeful.

q.t: Which author wrote Treasure Island, Kidnapped and Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde?
q.e: Robert Louis Stevenson (1850-94) wrote books which are still read by adults and children today. His most famous books include Treasure Island, Kidnapped and Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde.

q.t: Whose best-known novels focus on rural society and include Far from the Madding Crowd?
q.e: Thomas Hardy (1840-1928) was an author and poet. His best-known novels focus on rural society and include Far from the Madding Crowd and Jude the Obscure.

q.t: Sir Arthur Conan Doyle was a Scottish doctor best known for creating which character?
q.e: Sir Arthur Conan Doyle (1859-1930) was a Scottish doctor and writer. He was best known for his stories about Sherlock Holmes, who was one of the first fictional detectives.

q.t: Which of these statements is correct?
q.e: Sir Kingsley Amis was an English novelist and poet. He wrote more than 20 novels. The most well-known is Lucky Jim. Evelyn Waugh wrote satirical novels including Decline and Fall and Scoop, and is perhaps best known for Brideshead Revisited.
o: Sir Kingsley Amis wrote Lucky Jim

q.t: Which TWO British writers named in the handbook have won the Nobel Prize in Literature?
q.e: Several British writers, including the novelist Sir William Golding, the poet Seamus Heaney, and the playwright Harold Pinter, have won the Nobel Prize in Literature.

q.t: Which novel was voted the country's best-loved novel in 2003?
q.e: Agatha Christie's detective stories are read all over the world and Ian Fleming's books introduced James Bond. In 2003, The Lord of the Rings by JRR Tolkien was voted the country's best-loved novel.

q.t: Since which year has the Man Booker Prize for Fiction been awarded, and to whom?
q.e: The Man Booker Prize for Fiction is awarded annually for the best fiction novel written by an author from the Commonwealth, Ireland or Zimbabwe. It has been awarded since 1968.
o: Since 1968, to an author from the Commonwealth, Ireland or Zimbabwe
Since 1984, to an author from the Commonwealth, Ireland or Zimbabwe
Since 1968, to any author writing in English
Since 1927, to an author from the UK and Ireland

q.t: How many lines must a sonnet have?
q.e: As well as plays, Shakespeare wrote many sonnets, poems which must be 14 lines long, and some longer poems.

q.t: Which Anglo-Saxon poem tells of its hero's battles against monsters?
q.e: British poetry is among the richest in the world. The Anglo-Saxon poem Beowulf tells of its hero's battles against monsters and is still translated into modern English.
o: Sir Gawain and the Green Knight

q.t: Which poem from the Middle Ages is about one of the knights at the court of King Arthur?
q.e: Poems which survive from the Middle Ages include Chaucer's Canterbury Tales and a poem called Sir Gawain and the Green Knight, about one of the knights at the court of King Arthur.
o: Sir Gawain and the Green Knight

q.t: Who wrote Paradise Lost?
q.e: As Protestant ideas spread, a number of poets wrote poems inspired by their religious views. One of these was John Milton, who wrote Paradise Lost.

q.t: Which TWO poets were inspired to write about their experiences in the First World War?
q.e: Later, many poets, for example Wilfred Owen and Siegfried Sassoon, were inspired to write about their experiences in the First World War. More recently, popular poets have included Sir Walter de la Mare, John Masefield, Sir John Betjeman and Ted Hughes.

q.t: Where are some of the best-known poets buried or commemorated?
q.e: Some of the best-known poets are buried or commemorated in Poet's Corner in Westminster Abbey.

q.t: Which of these statements is correct?
q.e: William Wordsworth wrote 'I wander'd lonely as a cloud'. William Blake wrote 'Tyger! Tyger! Burning bright'. Sir Walter Scott wrote poems inspired by Scotland and the traditional stories and songs from the borders.
o: Sir Walter Scott wrote poems inspired by Scotland and border stories and songs
William Wordsworth wrote poems inspired by Scotland and border stories and songs

q.t: Which magazine, first published in the 1840s, was the most famous satirical magazine of the 19th century?
q.e: In the 19th century, satirical magazines began to be published. The most famous was Punch, which was published for the first time in the 1840s. Today, magazines such as Private Eye continue the tradition of satire.

q.t: Which programme introduced a new type of progressive comedy in 1969?
q.e: Satire has also continued to be important, with shows like That Was The Week That Was in the 1960s and Spitting Image in the 1980s and 1990s. In 1969, Monty Python's Flying Circus introduced a new type of progressive comedy.
o: That Was The Week That Was

q.t: Who told jokes and made fun of people in the court of medieval kings and rich nobles?
q.e: The traditions of comedy and satire, and the ability to laugh at ourselves, are an important part of the UK character. Medieval kings and rich nobles had jesters who told jokes and made fun of people in the Court.

q.t: Which German-born British artist is best known for his portraits?
q.e: Lucian Freud (1922-2011) was a German-born British artist. He is best known for his portraits. Henry Moore was an English sculptor best known for large bronze abstract sculptures.

q.t: Which of these statements is correct?
q.e: Ealing Studios has a claim to being the oldest continuously working film studio facility in the world. Some of the most commercially successful films of all time, including the two highest-grossing film franchises, Harry Potter and James Bond, have been produced in the UK.
o: Ealing Studios has a claim to being the oldest continuously working film studio in the world
Ealing Studios has a claim to being the largest film studio in the world

q.t: Which film directed by David Lean was released in 1962?
q.e: Some famous British films include Brief Encounter (1945), directed by David Lean; Lawrence of Arabia (1962), directed by David Lean; and The Third Man (1949), directed by Carol Reed.

q.t: What are the British Academy Film Awards the British equivalent of?
q.e: The annual British Academy Film Awards, hosted by the British Academy of Film and Television Arts (BAFTA), are the British equivalent of the Oscars.

q.t: Which director left for Hollywood and remained an important film director until his death in 1980?
q.e: British studios flourished in the 1930s. Eminent directors included Sir Alexander Korda and Sir Alfred Hitchcock, who later left for Hollywood and remained an important film director until his death in 1980.
